title: Help Paying for Electricity
intro: Maine has new help for electric bills this fall. Most Westbrook homes get power from Central Maine Power (CMP). Check your bill to be sure. Then follow the steps below.

emergency.title: Worried about a shutoff?
emergency.text: Call your electric company first. For CMP:
emergency.text2: Still stuck? Call the state's Consumer Assistance office:
emergency.hours2: Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.
emergency.dangerText: Call 911. For help finding other aid any time, dial 211.

who.title: Who may qualify
who.text: Most electric help is for households with lower incomes. You may qualify if you are approved for heating help (HEAP), or you get SNAP, TANF or MaineCare, or your income is at or below 150% of the federal poverty level.
who.fine: Heating help and electric help use many of the same papers. If you apply for one, ask about the other.

checklist.title: Get these ready
items: Your latest electric bill, with your account number
Proof of income, or letters about SNAP, TANF or MaineCare
Names and birth dates for everyone in your home
checklist.note: The electric bill must be in the name of someone in your home. Each program may ask for more, so check its official page.

steps.title: Last stop
steps.sub: Only when other programs are not enough

programs.name: The Opportunity Alliance
programs.summary: The local Community Action Agency for Cumberland County, which includes Westbrook. It helps with electric programs, and with heating help. Call first to make an appointment. Please do not walk in.

programs.name: Low Income Assistance Program (LIAP)
programs.summary: A monthly discount on your electric bill. Starting this fall, many CMP customers who qualify are signed up without having to apply.
programs.know: The state says CMP discounts run from 25% to 81% of the bill, based on income. Look for it on your November bill or later. No discount and you think you qualify? Call CMP, or ask the local agency. You can choose to opt out.

programs.name: CMP payment help
programs.summary: CMP can set up a payment plan if you are behind. It also has programs for people with medical needs.
programs.know: Ask about payment plans, SimplePay and medical emergency protection. You can call, or sign in to My Account online.

programs.name: Arrearage Management Program (AMP)
programs.summary: Helps erase an old electric bill. Over 12 months, part of what you owe is wiped out each month you pay on time. CMP says up to $500 a month.
programs.know: This is for people behind on their bill who are in the LIAP or HEAP programs. Ask the local agency if you qualify.

programs.name: Winter shutoff protection
programs.summary: From Nov 15 to Apr 15, an electric company must get the state's permission before it can shut off a home's power.
programs.know: Call your electric company first and ask for a payment plan. Still worried? Call the state at 800-452-4699, Monday to Friday, 9 to 4. They do not take walk-ins.

programs.name: Efficiency Maine rebates
programs.summary: Rebates on heat pumps, insulation and other upgrades can lower your energy use. Lower-income households get the biggest rebates.
programs.know: Rebate amounts can change, so check the official page or call before you buy.

programs.name: 211 Maine
programs.summary: A free help line that can point you to utility help near you.
programs.know: You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211.

programs.name: Veterans’ emergency help
programs.summary: Maine has an emergency money program for veterans. The state says it can help with rent, utilities and other urgent costs.
programs.know: Ask if your electric bill counts, then apply with the form on the official page. The state’s Public Advocate also lists Veterans Forward (347-443-0005) and USA Cares (1-800-773-0387) for veterans who are behind on bills.

programs.name: Westbrook General Assistance
programs.summary: City help for basic needs like heat and electricity when other programs are not enough. Appointment only, no walk-ins.
programs.know: Based on income for 30 days at a time. You must apply to other programs first.
